page: Microsoft Azure D64as_v5 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the DASv5 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 64 dedicated x86_64 vCPUs derived from 32 physical cores of an AMD EPYC 7763 processor operating at 3.525 GHz. The system is equipped with 256.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced allocation of 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. Local storage is absent on this instance, though it is compatible with external Premium Storage options.

Benchmark results place the D64as_v5 in the top 25% for multi-core processing, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 86388.11 and a PassMark CPU score of 62203.54. Memory subsystem performance is highly rated, with the PassMark memory score reaching the top 10% tier at 3100.34, and small-block cached read bandwidth measured at 4149.44 GB/sec. However, large-block uncached read and write memory bandwidths drop to average levels at 116.2 GB/sec and 58.21 GB/sec respectively. Single-core performance also falls into the average category, as evidenced by a Geekbench single-core score of 1595.0.

Given its high core density and balanced memory-to-vCPU ratio, this instance is suitable for multi-threaded workloads such as software compilation, database operations, and small-scale language model inference. It achieved 39290.0 on the Geekbench Clang compilation test and 63.24 million operations per second in Redis SET benchmarks. The lack of local storage and average single-threaded performance represent tradeoffs, making it less optimal for single-core bound applications or workloads requiring high-speed local scratch disks. Qualitatively, the instance offers resource density suitable for enterprise-scale general-purpose applications and container orchestration.
